title: The Star That Sent a 'Warning' Signal Before It Exploded
hook: Astronomers detected a strange pulse from a distant star—hours later, it vanished in a supernova, as if it was saying goodbye.
why_this_can_go_viral: The idea of a star 'communicating' its death triggers both fear and wonder, perfect for viral curiosity.

title: The Rogue Black Hole That's Headed Straight for Us
hook: A rogue black hole is barreling through the Milky Way at 5 million mph—and our solar system is in its path.
why_this_can_go_viral: Imminent cosmic doom is a proven viral driver; the specificity of 'headed for us' amplifies urgency.

title: The Declassified DARPA Report: 'We Shut Down a Time Loop in Space'
hook: DARPA allegedly observed a region of space where time repeated every 47 minutes—and then classified it forever.
why_this_can_go_viral: Conspiracy + time manipulation + classified documents = irresistible curiosity gap.

title: The Extinction Event That Erased All Sound From Earth
hook: After a gamma ray burst hit 450 million years ago, the planet went silent—no animal could hear for a thousand years.
why_this_can_go_viral: The eerie concept of a 'silent Earth' taps into sensory fear and extinction fascination.

title: The Dark Matter 'Vortex' That's Sucking Galaxies Into Oblivion
hook: A massive dark matter vortex is pulling entire galaxies into a void—and the Milky Way is drifting toward it.
why_this_can_go_viral: Visual of a 'vortex' is terrifying and easy to imagine; stakes are galactic in scale.

title: The Fermi Paradox Answer: 'They're Sleeping Until We're Ready'
hook: Aliens aren't ignoring us—they're in cryogenic hibernation, waiting for humanity to evolve enough to be worth waking for.
why_this_can_go_viral: Combines mystery with a dark, passive-aggressive twist on alien intelligence—high shareability.

title: The Asteroid That 'Woke Up' and Changed Course Toward Earth
hook: An asteroid suddenly altered its orbit to head straight for Earth—astronomers call it the 'awakening.'
why_this_can_go_viral: The word 'awakening' implies intent, turning a random rock into a conscious threat.

title: The Extinction Event That 'Burned' the Sky for a Million Years
hook: After a supernova 2.6 million years ago, the sky glowed red continuously—and Earth's climate never recovered.
why_this_can_go_viral: Visual imagery of a permanently burning sky is haunting and shareable.

title: The Stellar Danger: A 'Vampire' Star That Drains Its Neighbor to Explode
hook: A white dwarf is siphoning gas from a nearby star—when it reaches critical mass, it'll detonate as a supernova.
why_this_can_go_viral: The 'vampire' metaphor is instantly gripping and translates well to short-form video.

title: The Dark Matter 'Wall' That's Blocking Our View of the Universe
hook: A massive dark matter structure is hiding 40% of the observable universe behind it—we'll never see what's there.
why_this_can_go_viral: The idea of a hidden, forbidden region of space taps into deep curiosity and paranoia.

title: The Fermi Paradox Answer: 'We're in a Simulation—And the Server Is Dying'
hook: Physicists noticed the universe's constants are subtly changing—as if the simulation hosting us is corrupting.
why_this_can_go_viral: Simulation theory is massively popular, and the 'dying server' angle adds urgent horror.

title: The Declassified Soviet File: 'We Lost a Cosmonaut to a Space Anomaly'
hook: A Soviet cosmonaut reportedly floated into a 'hole in space' and was never seen again—the mission was scrubbed from records.
why_this_can_go_viral: Lost cosmonaut conspiracies are evergreen; the 'hole in space' detail elevates it.

title: The Rogue Planet That 'Stole' an Atmosphere From a Living World
hook: A rogue planet ripped the atmosphere off a nearby exoplanet and now wears it like a ghostly cloak.
why_this_can_go_viral: The anthropomorphic 'theft' narrative makes a complex event feel personal and dramatic.

title: The Strange Cosmic Signal That 'Matches' the Voyager Golden Record
hook: A signal from a distant star perfectly matches the binary encoding of the Voyager Golden Record—almost as if it's a reply.
why_this_can_go_viral: The idea that aliens answered our message is a universal sci-fi fantasy—now with real data.

title: The Asteroid That 'Splits' Into Two Before Hitting—Every Time
hook: A binary asteroid system always separates before impact—each fragment hits a different continent with surgical precision.
why_this_can_go_viral: The 'surgical precision' angle implies intelligence behind the pattern—terrifying and mysterious.

title: The Stellar Danger: A 'Cannibal' Star That Eats Other Stars Whole
hook: A massive star was caught devouring a smaller companion—leaving only a glowing scar where the other star once orbited.
why_this_can_go_viral: Cannibalism in space is an immediate attention-grabber with strong visual potential.

title: The Dark Matter 'Shadow' That Moves Against the Galaxies
hook: Something invisible is moving through the universe against the flow of galaxies—it's called the 'anti-shadow.'
why_this_can_go_viral: The concept of a 'shadow' with intent is deeply unsettling and easy to animate.

title: The Fermi Paradox Answer: 'They Sealed Themselves in a Black Hole'
hook: A hyper-advanced civilization may have retreated into a black hole to escape a dying universe—their last refuge.
why_this_can_go_viral: A dark, desperate answer to the Fermi paradox—high emotional impact and philosophical depth.

title: The Declassified CIA File: 'We Saw a Star Go Out—Then Come Back'
hook: A star dimmed to zero luminosity for 6 months, then reignited—the CIA monitored it but never explained how.
why_this_can_go_viral: Mystery + government involvement + violation of known physics = perfect viral cocktail.
